readings.title: The Invitation of Pharaoh
readings.subtitle: Pharaoh Welcomes Joseph's Family
readings.text: [Genesis 45:16] And the report was heard in Par'oh’s house, saying, “Yoseph’s brothers have come.” And it was good in the eyes of Par'oh and in the eyes of his servants. [17] And Par'oh said to Yoseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: Load <dn>את</dn> your beasts and go, enter the land of Kena’an, [18] and take <dn>את</dn> your father and <dn>את</dn> your households and come to me, and I give you the best of the land of Mitsrayim, and you eat the fat of the land.’ [19] And you, you have been commanded, do this: ‘Take <dn>את</dn> wagons out of the land of Mitsrayim for your little ones and for your wives, and you shall bring <dn>את</dn> your father and come. [20] And do not let your eye pity your goods, for the best of all the land of Mitsrayim is yours.’ ” [21] And the sons of Yisra’el did so. And Yoseph gave them wagons, according to the mouth of Par'oh, and he gave them food for the way. [22] To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of garments, but to Benyamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments. [23] And to his father he sent this: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Mitsrayim, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and food for his father for the way. [24] So he sent <dn>את</dn> his brothers away, and they left. And he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way.” [25] And they went up out of Mitsrayim, and came into the land of Kena’an to Ya’aqoḇ their father. [26] And they told him, saying, “Yoseph is still alive, and he is governor over all the land of Mitsrayim.” And Ya’aqoḇ’s heart fainted, for he did not believe them. [27] But when they told him <dn>את</dn> all the words of Yoseph which he had spoken to them, and when he saw <dn>את</dn> the wagons which Yoseph had sent to bring him, the spirit of Ya’aqoḇ their father revived. [28] And Yisra’el said, “It is enough! Yoseph my son is still alive. Let me go and see him before I die.”

readings.title: Israel Moves to Egypt
readings.subtitle: The Journey to Egypt
readings.text: [Genesis 46:1] And Yisra’el set out with all that he had, and came to Be’ĕrsheba, and offered slaughterings to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of his father Yitsḥaq. [2] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Yisra’el in the visions of the night, and said, <dq>“Ya’aqoḇ, Ya’aqoḇ!”</dq> And he said, “Here I am.” [3] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Ěl</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Mitsrayim, for <dn>I</dn> make you a great nation there.</dq> [4] <dq><dn>I Myself</dn> go down with you to Mitsrayim, and <dn>I Myself</dn> certainly bring you up again. And let Yoseph put his hand on your eyes.”</dq> [5] And Ya’aqoḇ rose up from Be’ĕrsheba. And the sons of Yisra’el brought <dn>את</dn> Ya’aqoḇ their father, and <dn>את</dn> their little ones, and <dn>את</dn> their wives, in the wagons which Par'oh had sent to bring <dn>את</dn> him. [6] And they took <dn>את</dn> their livestock and <dn>את</dn> their goods which they had acquired in the land of Kena’an, and came to Mitsrayim, Ya’aqoḇ and all his seed with him. [7] His sons and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters and his sons’ daughters and <dn>את</dn> all his seed he brought with him to Mitsrayim. [8] And these are the names of the sons of Yisra’el who came into Mitsrayim: Ya’aqoḇ and his sons. Re’uḇĕn was Ya’aqoḇ’s first-born. [9] And the sons of Re’uḇĕn: Ḥanoḵ, and Pallu, and Ḥetsron, and Karmi. [10] And the sons of Shim’on: Yemu’ĕl, and Yamin, and Ohaḏ, and Yaḵin, and Tsoḥar, and Sha’ul, the son of a Kena’anite woman. [11] And the sons of Lĕwi: Gĕreshon, Qehath, and Merari. [12] And the sons of Yehuḏah: Ěr, and Onan, and Shĕlah, and Perets, and Zeraḥ. But Ěr and Onan died in the land of Kena’an. And the sons of Perets were Ḥetsron and Hamul. [13] And the sons of Yissaḵar: Tola, and Puvvah, and Iyoḇ, and Shimron. [14] And the sons of Zeḇulun: Sereḏ, and Ělon, and Yaḥle’ĕl. [15] These were the sons of Lĕ’ah, whom she bore to Ya’aqoḇ in Paddan Aram, with <dn>את</dn> his daughter Dinah. All the beings, his sons and his daughters, were thirty-three. [16] And the sons of Gaḏ: Tsiphion, and Ḥaggi, Shuni, and Ezḇon, Ěri, and Aroḏi, and Arĕli. [17] And the sons of Ashĕr: Yimnah, and Yishwah, and Yishwi, and Beri’ah, and Seraḥ their sister. And the sons of Beri’ah: Ḥeḇer and Malki’ĕl. [18] These were the sons of Zilpah, whom Laḇan gave to Lĕ’ah his daughter. And she bore these to Ya’aqoḇ: <dn>את</dn> sixteen beings. [19] The sons of Raḥĕl, Ya’aqoḇ’s wife: Yoseph and Benyamin. [20] And to Yoseph in the land of Mitsrayim were born <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh and <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Phera priest of On, bore to him. [21] And the sons of Benyamin: Bela, and Beḵer, and Ashḇĕl, Gĕra, and Na’aman, Ěḥi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Ḥuppim, and Arḏ. [22] These were the sons of Raḥĕl, who were born to Ya’aqoḇ: fourteen beings in all. [23] And the son of Dan: Ḥushim. [24] And the sons of Naphtali: Yaḥtse’ĕl, and Guni, and Yĕtser, and Shillĕm. [25] These were the sons of Bilhah, whom Laḇan gave to Raḥĕl his daughter. And she bore these to Ya’aqoḇ: <dn>את</dn> seven beings in all. [26] All the beings who went with Ya’aqoḇ to Mitsrayim, who came from his body, besides Ya’aqoḇ’s sons’ wives, were sixty-six beings in all. [27] And the sons of Yoseph who were born to him in Mitsrayim were two beings. All the beings of the house of Ya’aqoḇ who came to Mitsrayim were seventy.

readings.title: The Reunion in Goshen
readings.subtitle: Reunion in Goshen
readings.text: [Genesis 46:28] And he sent <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah before him to Yoseph, to point out before him the way to Goshen. And they came into the land of Goshen. [29] And Yoseph made ready <dn>את</dn> his chariot and went up to Goshen to meet his father Yisra’el. And he appeared to him, and fell on his neck and wept on his neck a long time. [30] And Yisra’el said to Yoseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.” [31] And Yoseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I am going up to inform Par'oh, and say to him, ‘My brothers and my father’s household, who were in the land of Kena’an, have come to me. [32] And the men are shepherds, for they have been men of livestock. And they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’ [33] And it shall be, when Par'oh calls you and says, ‘What is your occupation?’ [34] that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been men of livestock from our youth even until now, both we and also our fathers,’ so that you dwell in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is an abomination to the Mitsrites.”

readings.title: Jacob Before Pharaoh
readings.subtitle: Jacob Before Pharaoh
readings.text: [Genesis 47:1] And Yoseph came and informed Par'oh, and said, “My father and my brothers, and their flocks and their herds and all that they have, have come from the land of Kena’an. And see, they are in the land of Goshen.” [2] And he took five men from among his brothers and presented them to Par'oh. [3] And Par'oh said to his brothers, “What is your occupation?” And they said to Par'oh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we and also our fathers.” [4] And they said to Par'oh, “We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks, for the scarcity of food is severe in the land of Kena’an. And now, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.” [5] And Par'oh spoke to Yoseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you. [6] The land of Mitsrayim is before you. Settle <dn>את</dn> your father and <dn>את</dn> your brothers in the best of the land, let them dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know of any capable men among them, then make them chief herdsmen over my livestock.” [7] And Yoseph brought in <dn>את</dn> Ya’aqoḇ his father and set him before Par'oh. And Ya’aqoḇ blessed <dn>את</dn> Par'oh. [8] And Par'oh said to Ya’aqoḇ, “How many are the days of the years of your life?” [9] And Ya’aqoḇ said to Par'oh, “The days of the years of my sojourning are one hundred and thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojourning.” [10] And Ya’aqoḇ blessed <dn>את</dn> Par'oh, and went out from before Par'oh. [11] And Yoseph settled <dn>את</dn> his father and <dn>את</dn> his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Mitsrayim, in the best of the land, in the land of Ra’amses, as Par'oh had commanded. [12] And Yoseph provided <dn>את</dn> his father, and <dn>את</dn> his brothers, and <dn>את</dn> all his father’s household with bread, according to the mouth of the little ones.

readings.title: The Famine Tightens
readings.subtitle: Joseph Manages the Famine
readings.text: [Genesis 47:13] Now there was no bread in all the land, for the scarcity of food was very severe, so that the land of Mitsrayim and the land of Kena’an exhausted themselves because of the scarcity of food. [14] And Yoseph gathered up <dn>את</dn> all the silver that was found in the land of Mitsrayim and in the land of Kena’an, for the grain which they bought. And Yoseph brought <dn>את</dn> the silver into Par'oh’s house. [15] And when the silver was all spent in the land of Mitsrayim and in the land of Kena’an, all the Mitsrites came to Yoseph and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die before your eyes? For the silver is gone!” [16] And Yoseph said, “Give <dn>את</dn> your livestock, and I give you bread for your livestock, if the silver is gone.” [17] So they brought <dn>את</dn> their livestock to Yoseph, and Yoseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the cattle of the herds, and for the donkeys. Thus he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock that year. [18] And when that year had ended, they came to him the next year and said to him, “We do not hide from my lord that our silver is spent, and my lord has our livestock. There is no one left before my lord but our bodies and our land. [19] Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy <dn>את</dn> us and <dn>את</dn> our land for bread, and let us and our land be servants of Par'oh. And give us seed, and let us live and not die, and let the land not be a waste.” [20] And Yoseph bought <dn>את</dn> all the land of Mitsrayim for Par'oh, for every Mitsrite sold <dn>את</dn> his field, because the scarcity of food was severe upon them. And the land became Par'oh’s. [21] And as for <dn>את</dn> the people, he moved them into the cities, from one end of the borders of Mitsrayim even to the other end. [22] Only <dn>את</dn> the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a portion from Par'oh, and they ate <dn>את</dn> their portion which Par'oh gave them. Therefore they did not sell <dn>את</dn> their land. [23] And Yoseph said to the people, “See, I have bought <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your land today for Par'oh. See, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land. [24] And it shall be in the harvest that you shall give one-fifth to Par'oh, and four-fifths is your own, as seed for the field and for your food, and for those of your households and as food for your little ones.” [25] And they said, “You have saved <dn>את</dn> our lives. Let us find favour in the eyes of my lord, and we shall be Par'oh’s servants.” [26] And Yoseph made it a law over the land of Mitsrayim to this day, that Par'oh should have one-fifth, except for the land of the priests only, which did not become Par'oh’s. [27] And Yisra’el dwelt in the land of Mitsrayim, in the land of Goshen. And they had possessions in it, and were fruitful and increased exceedingly.
